sources.title: Anthropic Claude Fable 5.1 / Mythos 5.1 (identity, availability, coding)
sources.role: Discovery-bounded source used for factual verification

claims.text: Anthropic introduced Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 in September 2026 as the same model with different safeguard levels: Fable 5.1 generally available, Mythos 5.1 via trusted access programs for cybersecurity and life-sciences work.
claims.context: First-party announcement consumed; availability split (GA vs CVP/LSVP with US-government life-sciences partnership) as stated.

claims.text: Fable 5.1 pricing: cache reads $0.25/MTok (75% reduction), ~25% cheaper typical token-billed workloads and up to ~45% cheaper on highly agentic work; otherwise $10/M input and $50/M output; API id claude-fable-5-1.
claims.context: Vendor-stated pricing arithmetic; realized savings depend on workload mix.

claims.text: Vendor-reported benchmark deltas include Terminal-Bench-Science 52.6%, Terminal-Bench 4.0 55.8% (Mythos 60.9%), GDPval-AA v2 1853, OSWorld 2.0 partial 77.9% / strict 41.7%, AutomationBench 31.4%, CursorBench 73.4%.
claims.context: Lab-reported figures from the announcement page; externally unreproduced.

claims.text: Safety posture as stated: Mythos chem/bio capability above Mythos 5 but below the next RSP risk tier; strongest Anthropic cyber capabilities in a lower FCF risk category with no critical jailbreak found; biology safeguards fire 85% less on benign queries and cyber safeguards average ~60% fewer interventions.
claims.context: Vendor safety-framework self-assessment; evaluation details not yet observable.

limitations.text: All benchmark and safety-evaluation figures are lab-reported and externally unreproduced.
limitations.context: Evidence boundary retained for downstream editorial use.

limitations.text: Mythos vetting criteria and watermark detection API preview scope are announced programs, not observed deployments.
limitations.context: Evidence boundary retained for downstream editorial use.

limitations.text: Science anecdotes are vendor-selected case reports, not controlled evidence.
